title: A metric with no local isometric immersion
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: A smooth metric on a square can fail to be the metric of any smooth surface in three-dimensional space, on every neighbourhood of a point: this is a theorem of OpenAI (2026). The first lesson proves three tools for arbitrary isometric immersions: the height equation (the height of an immersed surface in a fixed direction satisfies det Hess z = K det g (1 - |dz|^2)), the construction of a metric dX^2 + f^2 dY^2 with a given small curvature, and the fact that a graph whose curvature is negative in a disk and zero on its boundary has a boundary point where the second fundamental form has rank one. The second lesson constructs the metric and proves the theorem from one named statement, the patch obstruction (P): near a model metric with curvature kappa (x^2 - h(y)) on the square [-3, 3]^2 there are metrics for which the height equation has no admissible solution on the whole square. Small copies of such squares in finitely many orientations accumulate at every boundary point of disks of negative curvature, the disks accumulate at the origin, and all pieces add up to one smooth metric with the Taylor series of the Euclidean metric at the origin. The statement (P) is the analytic part of OpenAI's proof. The third lesson begins the analytic part: it derives, as exact identities, the linear equation satisfied by a derivative of high order of a solution of the height equation: the drift identity for the direction in which the Hessian degenerates, and the equation u_tt + A u_ss + B u_t + C u_s = R in flow coordinates, with A the curvature times a positive function and C = (l + 1) A_s up to an explicit multiple of the curvature. The estimates built on this equation, and with them the proof of (P), are not yet in the course.
prerequisites: the lesson Submanifolds and hypersurfaces (course Bundles, curvature and holonomy), Proposition A.3: the Gauss formula in coordinates and the Gaussian curvature as det II / det g
core course Real Analysis: differentiation under the integral, uniform convergence of series of derivatives, the inverse function theorem
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the patch obstruction (P), which is a named hypothesis of the second lesson

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A Smooth Metric with No Local Isometric Immersion into Three-Space' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026) was read in full on 12 Oct 2026 (introduction, model, caps, pulse, assembly; 1,512 lines of TeX). Lesson 1 was written against the lemma 'Height equation' (Section 2), the lemma 'Prescribing small curvature' and the lemma 'A negatively curved disk' (Section 5). Every step was derived. The lesson adds: the transformation rules under affine maps with proof, a complete proof of the smoothness of the solution of f_XX = -K_0 f in both variables (the manuscript refers to smooth dependence on a parameter), and the reduction of an immersion that is a graph to the graph of a function (the manuscript uses the formula for graphs directly). Checked in exact arithmetic before staging (plan/checks_20261012/ni_check_heights.py): K = -f_XX/f from the coordinate formula; for a polynomial graph and four vectors e, the Gauss equation, Hess z = nu II, the height equation and nu^2 + |dz|^2 = |e|^2; the rules H' = lambda^2 R^T H R, E' = lambda^4 E, K' = K under an affine map. No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 2 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the definitions and the statement of the proposition 'Patch obstruction' in Section 2 and against Section 5 (placement and smooth summation, the proof of the main theorem, the corollary on the Euclidean Taylor jet). Every step of Section 5 was derived. The lesson makes the placement explicit (circles of radius rho_j (1 + 2^-k) with A 2^k equally spaced centres and rotations assigned cyclically; the inequalities for disjointness are verified), gives the bound for the push-forward of a perturbation with its constant, and states the consequence of the proposition that the construction uses as statement (P). No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 3 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the lemmas 'Curvature drift' and 'High derivative equation' of Section 3. Every identity was derived; the terms written O(K) in the manuscript are explicit in the lesson (rho_1, rho_2, rho, and the multiple of K in C). Checked by computer algebra before staging: plan/checks_20261012/ni_check_commutation.py (the commutation of third derivatives with its sign, exact, three random metrics), ni_check_drift.py (the drift identity with rho_1 and rho_2, exact, on the height of a polynomial graph at three points; the partial derivatives of P, symbolic), ni_check_multiplier.py (the formula for D^2 and the differentiated equation, symbolic). The manuscript's formulas agree with the explicit ones.
checks.layout: Measured on 12 Oct 2026 in the staged pages at widths 1100, 768, 543 and 375 px: lesson 3 has 388 formulas, lesson 2 has 438, lesson 1 has 341; none wider than its column, no formula errors, no horizontal page scroll.

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (P), the patch obstruction (the proposition 'Patch obstruction' of Section 2 of the manuscript, in the form: for every model metric g_0, every m and every epsilon > 0 there is a perturbation eta supported in [-1/10, 1/10]^2 with C^m norm below epsilon such that g_0 + eta is positive definite and has no admissible height). Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 6.1 of the second lesson are proved from it. Of its proof (Sections 3 and 4 of the manuscript) the course contains the identities of the third lesson (the drift identity and the differentiated equation in flow coordinates). Not in the course: the bound of the remainder R_l by Sobolev inequalities; the estimate at the free edge of a cap (a directed multiplier where K <= c_1 d and a weighted elliptic estimate where K >= c_1 d; its algebraic identities were checked by computer algebra, its estimates not yet line by line); the induction on the order of derivatives; hyperbolic energy estimates in the slab of negative curvature; the Taylor comparison across the thin strip and the oscillatory moment; the Baire category argument in the space of smooth perturbations.

Foundations that a proof of (P) in the course would use and that should be checked in the programme first: Sobolev inequalities on plane domains and on intervals, energy estimates for linear hyperbolic equations of second order in two variables, the theorem of Baire for the space of smooth functions with compact support in a fixed square.
free_sources: OpenAI, A smooth metric with no local isometric immersion into three-space (OpenAI Math Release preprint, 24 Sep 2026), Sections 1, 2, 3 and 5
